historical_scope_v5_superseded.summary: Resolve the diff-hash vs Yjs-update-hash conflation that makes an approved-proposal-backed (Proposal-kind) CRDT ModelLaneMessage un-admittable, so proposal-anchored CRDT authority can be proven end-to-end.
historical_scope_v5_superseded.root_cause: apply_approved_ai_edit (src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/ai_edit_proposal.rs ~665-691) computes applied_content_sha256 = sha256(serde_json::to_vec(applied_diff)) — a hash of the JSON diff object. bind_applied_ai_edit_update (src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/knowledge_crdt.rs ~1562-1586) and migration 0192's CHECK force applied_update_sha256 = diff_sha256, i.e. that same JSON hash. But resolve_model_lane_crdt_authority_tx (src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs ~13011,13073-13085) requires the referenced kernel_crdt_updates row to satisfy BOTH sha256(update_bytes) == update_sha256 AND Update::decode_v1(update_bytes) succeeds — i.e. update_sha256 is the hash of the Yjs v1 BINARY update. Then the proposal cross-check (~13784-13793) requires proposal.applied_update_sha256 == resolved.update_sha256. Equating a JSON-object hash with a Yjs-binary hash is unsatisfiable short of a SHA-256 collision, so no honest proposal row can ever back an admitted CRDT message.

historical_scope_v5_superseded.root_cause_addendum_2026_07_30: SECOND INDEPENDENT BLOCKER, omitted from root_cause above and VERIFIED at source: apply_approved_ai_edit also blocks BEFORE the resolver is ever reached. ai_edit_proposal.rs:702-709 calls knowledge_crdt::find_applied_crdt_update_sha256, which SELECTs kernel_crdt_updates.update_sha256 (knowledge_crdt.rs:1597-1623) — the Yjs-BINARY hash. Line 710 then compares that against applied_content_sha256, the JSON-diff hash computed at line 691. So the binder can only ever stamp a row when the persisted update_bytes ARE the JSON diff bytes, which then cannot decode as Yjs v1 at model_lane.rs:13123. Fixing only the resolver cross-check leaves the proposal un-mintable. The comment at ai_edit_proposal.rs:693-701 shows the INTENT was existence + row integrity; the implementation conflated the two hash spaces. Fix: make line 710 an existence check (stored_update_sha256.is_none()), still passing stored_update_sha256 into deny_applied_update_missing so the update_row_absent discriminator stays meaningful. Row integrity is already enforced by the resolver at model_lane.rs:13118-13127 and must not be duplicated.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Proposal diff_sha256 is computed over canonical approved-diff bytes; Yjs update_sha256 is computed independently over persisted Yjs v1 update bytes. The values remain distinct invariants, are never equated, and are independently recomputed before admission and replay.

AC-2: An approved and applied proposal binds to the real scoped update by applied_update_id while applied_update_sha256 remains the proposal's approved-diff hash; ModelLane separately verifies the cited update row's update_sha256, Yjs decoding, state-vector advance, causal chain, and terminal identity.

AC-3: Proposal record, approve/reject/promote transition, applied-update binding, CRDT update, snapshot, lease, ModelLane message, and denial/admission receipt use exact owner_account_id, actor_principal_id, authenticated_session_id, access_space_id, and workspace_id predicates on both resource and linked canonical-event rows.

AC-4: Scope derivation never widens. Mixed-source proposal inputs are refused rather than unioned, and each one-field mismatch, stale context, revoked context, incomplete row, malformed ref, or mixed-scope linked event returns no resource metadata and performs zero mutation.

AC-5: Every durable proposal/update/snapshot/lease/message/receipt mutation appends or links the canonical kernel EventLedger atomically in the same Surreal transaction; no domain-local audit island or event-without-resource/resource-without-event state is admissible.

AC-6: Proposal, ModelLane, CRDT update/snapshot, lease, receipt, and replay providers receive clones of one injected SurrealStorage namespace/database. Restart reopens that same authority and preserves both hashes, applied identity, canonical-event links, ordering, and idempotency.

AC-7: A real Proposal-kind ModelLaneMessage backed by an approved applied proposal, real persisted Yjs update, causally prior snapshot, active exact-scope lease, matching actor/session/trace/document identities, and complete CRDT fields is admitted and replays unchanged.

AC-8: Fabricated update/proposal refs, Yjs byte-hash mismatch, approved-diff mismatch, proposal bound to another real update, stale/unrelated vector or snapshot, wrong actor/session/trace/document, unapproved/rejected review state, missing applied binding, duplicate conflict, and tampered linked event all fail closed with stable denial taxonomy.

AC-9: One reusable Surreal admissible-CRDT helper constructs all positive authority only through production APIs and is reused by the MT-002, MT-005, MT-009, and MT-018 positive and negative proof surfaces; no raw insert may manufacture a green posture.

AC-10: The original provisional decision remains explicit: applied_update_sha256 names approved-diff integrity, applied_update_id names the real Yjs update, and the Yjs row owns its independent update_sha256. Any specification enrichment must preserve this separation.

historical_cancellation_defect_2026_08_0.headline: The two tests that HUNG the mixed suite are now bounded, and they resolve to ONE product defect: the coordinator cannot interrupt an in-progress factory create, so cancellation either blocks or fails to reach the worker.
historical_cancellation_defect_2026_08_0.before: ac9_cancel_and_peer_failure_propagate_into_blocked_factory_create and ac9_cancel_terminalizes_parallel_siblings_and_live_sessions never completed. 86 minutes elapsed for 62 CPU-seconds with every other test in the binary finished. historical_cancellation_defect_2026_08_0.change_made: Bounded both awaits with tokio::time::timeout(60s). NO assertion was altered, removed, or weakened - only the FAILURE MODE. A hang is not a more cautious outcome than a failed assertion; it is a worse one, because it destroys the suite's ability to report at all.

now_observed.ac9_cancel_and_peer_failure_propagate_in: FAILS with 'cancellation must propagate INTO the blocked factory create and end the worker: Elapsed'. cancel_routing_execution ITSELF returned successfully with status Cancelled - so the execution is marked cancelled while the worker stays stuck inside create().
now_observed.ac9_cancel_terminalizes_parallel_sibling: FAILS with 'cancel_routing_execution must not hang while siblings are live: Elapsed'. Here the cancel CALL itself never returns.

SINGLE_ROOT_CAUSE.diagnosis: The coordinator has no way to interrupt a ModelSessionFactory::create() that is already running. cancel_routing_execution collects the live instances (releasing the registry and pending_spawns locks BEFORE any await, so this is NOT a lock-across-await deadlock) and then awaits cancel_session per instance. For a session still inside create(), that await cannot complete.
SINGLE_ROOT_CAUSE.explains_both_symptoms: Symptom B is that await never returning. Symptom A is the same gap seen from the other side: the DB row is terminalized but the blocked create is never unwound, so the worker task never ends.
SINGLE_ROOT_CAUSE.test_side_confirmation: Ac9ProductionFactory::create blocks in `while hold_create || held_models.contains(model) { sleep(25ms) }` with no cancellation awareness, and the blocked-create test never clears hold_create. The fixture is deliberately constructed so that ONLY real cancellation propagation can break it out - which is precisely the behaviour AC-9 requires and which is missing.
SINGLE_ROOT_CAUSE.fix_shape_not_applied: Making create() cancellable - e.g. driving it under a tokio::select! against the coordinator-owned session cancel token, or running it as an abortable task whose handle cancellation aborts. This is a real change to the spawn admission path in coordinator.rs and was NOT attempted here: validating it requires the full mixed suite plus the swarm coordinator suites, which is hours of runtime, and a half-validated change to the spawn path is exactly how the regressions earlier in this session happened.

historical_cancellation_defect_2026_08_0.attribution_open: NOT established as pre-existing or regression. Unlike the TRUNCATE and proposal_ref failures - whose mechanisms were traced to COMMITTED sources (migration 0362 and model_lane.rs in HEAD) - no committed-vs-working-tree mechanism was traced for this one. Stating it either way would be a guess.

historical_cancellation_fix_2026_08_05_s.headline: PRODUCT FIX LANDED. The blocked-factory-create cancellation defect is FIXED and its test now PASSES (was an infinite hang). The sibling case is a SEPARATE defect, now narrowed to a precise mechanism.

fix_applied.was: On cancellation the spawn path did `(create.await, true)` - an UNBOUNDED wait for the in-flight factory create. The intent was sound and documented: a create may already have crossed an external side-effect boundary, so dropping it immediately could orphan a real process.
fix_applied.why_that_was_still_wrong: cancel_routing_execution awaits cancel_session for every live instance, so ONE factory create that never returns wedges the operator's cancel forever. An orphaned process is recoverable through the process-ledger reclaim path; a cancel that never returns is not recoverable by the operator at all. The bound was missing, not the intent.
fix_applied.now: The post-cancellation wait is bounded by config.teardown_timeout - the SAME budget that already bounds every other unwind in this coordinator (it also bounds the session teardown at coordinator.rs:4902), so no new magic constant was introduced. Within the grace the create still resolves and is compensated exactly as before; past it the create is abandoned with a typed FactoryFailed error naming the abandonment, and any external side effect is explicitly left to process-ledger reclaim.
fix_applied.proof: ac9_cancel_and_peer_failure_propagate_into_blocked_factory_create: 1 passed, 0 failed (45.91s). Before this change the same test never terminated. cargo check --features test-utils --all-targets: exit 0.

REMAINING_SEPARATE_DEFECT.status: STILL FAILS - 'cancel_routing_execution must not hang while siblings are live: Elapsed'.
REMAINING_SEPARATE_DEFECT.why_it_is_NOT_the_same_defect: This test sets hold_generation, NOT hold_create. Both factory creates COMPLETE (the test asserts creates == 2), so the sessions are LIVE and blocked inside GENERATION, not inside create. The fix above therefore cannot apply to it, and correctly did not change its result.
REMAINING_SEPARATE_DEFECT.narrowed_mechanism: cancel_session takes the live path -> terminate(). The session TEARDOWN is already bounded by teardown_timeout (coordinator.rs:4902), so teardown is not the unbounded step. What remains unbounded in terminate() are its DURABLE WRITES: the terminal-state write and record_lane_terminal_status. The most probable cause is that those writes block on PostgreSQL row locks still held by the generation work being cancelled - i.e. cancellation waiting on locks held by the very work it is trying to cancel.
REMAINING_SEPARATE_DEFECT.not_fixed_here: Deliberately not patched blind. Confirming it requires observing lock waits (pg_locks / pg_stat_activity) during the hang, and the fix shape - bounding those writes, or making the generation path release its transaction on cancel - changes durability behaviour on the terminal path. That is exactly the class of change that caused three regressions earlier in this session when made without full validation.
REMAINING_SEPARATE_DEFECT.next_concrete_step: Run the test while sampling pg_stat_activity for blocked queries on the model_lane rows to confirm the lock-wait hypothesis before changing the terminal write path.

historical_cancellation_fix_2026_08_05_s.harness_hardening_retained: Both tests keep their bounded tokio::time::timeout wrappers. No assertion was altered. Before this, these two tests hung forever and suppressed the failure reporting of the ENTIRE binary (libtest prints failure detail only at the end), which is why mixed_model_lane_integration_pg_tests could not serve as evidence and MT-017's capstone was unreachable. The suite now always reports.

historical_advisory_lock_cancellation_de.headline: ROOT CAUSE OF THE SIBLING CANCELLATION HANG, established from LIVE PostgreSQL evidence, not inference: a pg_advisory_xact_lock is held across an in-process await, so cancellation queues behind the very work it is cancelling.
historical_advisory_lock_cancellation_de.how_it_was_established: The test was run while sampling pg_stat_activity and pg_blocking_pids during the hang window. This replaced two earlier hypotheses that were both WRONG and are recorded as refuted below.

observed_blocking_chain.88652: wait_event = Client/ClientRead, blocked_by = {} -- THE HOLDER. Its last statement is `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0))`, so it took the advisory lock and then went IDLE IN TRANSACTION waiting on the application. It is not waiting on PostgreSQL at all; it is parked awaiting Rust.

historical_advisory_lock_cancellation_de.mechanism: swarm_orchestration/routing_execution.rs defines `lock_execution` (line 2554) which issues pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(execution_id, 0)) INSIDE a transaction, and it is called from EIGHT sites (lines 345, 369, 507, 716, 1256, 1822, 1982, 2221) including claim_ready (709) and record_generated_output (1566). Because the lock is an XACT lock it is held until that transaction ends. When a stage is mid-generation the holding transaction stays open across the generation await, and cancel_routing_execution - which needs the same execution-keyed advisory lock to terminalize - blocks behind it indefinitely. The advisory lock serializes on execution_id, so a slow or blocked stage makes the operator's cancel unreachable by construction.
historical_advisory_lock_cancellation_de.why_the_other_symptom_differed: ac9_cancel_and_peer_failure_propagate_into_blocked_factory_create used hold_create, so the stall was in factory create BEFORE any generation transaction existed; bounding the post-cancel create wait (the fix already landed) resolved it and that test now passes. ac9_cancel_terminalizes_parallel_siblings_and_live_sessions uses hold_generation instead: both creates COMPLETE, the sessions are live, and the stall is inside generation while a routing transaction holds the advisory lock. Same visible symptom, genuinely different cause - which is why the first fix correctly did not mask the second.
hypotheses_raised_and_REFUTED: REFUTED: 'terminate() never fires the session cancel token, so generation never stops.' It does - coordinator.rs:4645 calls handle.cancel.cancel(), and the fixture's generate() stream polls cancel.is_cancelled() every 25ms and emits ModelRuntimeError::Cancelled.
REFUTED: 'the session teardown await is unbounded.' It is already bounded by config.teardown_timeout at coordinator.rs:4902 (5s default).

REFUTED (earlier, separately): 'the ledger writer STOP identity hardening broke external reclaim.' ProcessReclaim::reclaim_stop derives its STOP identity from the persisted row, so it stays byte-identical.
historical_advisory_lock_cancellation_de.fix_shape_NOT_applied: The advisory lock must not span a model-generation await. Options: (a) take the lock, perform the state transition, COMMIT, and re-acquire for the post-generation write, so the lock is held only for the duration of a durable transition rather than the duration of inference; or (b) give cancellation a lock-free terminalization path so an operator cancel never queues behind stage work. Not applied here because it changes transactional boundaries on the routing terminal path - the exact class of change that produced three regressions earlier in this session when landed without full-suite validation, and the full mixed suite plus swarm suites are hours of runtime.
historical_advisory_lock_cancellation_de.severity: Operator-facing. Any cancel of a routing execution whose stage is mid-generation will block for the duration of that generation. With a real model rather than a test fixture that is a long, unexplained UI stall on the cancel path.

historical_transaction_across_generation.headline: CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE. The advisory lock was a SYMPTOM. The actual defect is that the routing wave holds a PostgreSQL transaction OPEN ACROSS MODEL GENERATION, so every concurrent operation - including operator cancellation - queues behind inference.
historical_transaction_across_generation.correction_of_my_earlier_claim: An earlier record in this MT stated the advisory lock held across an await was the root cause, and a later message claimed 'the deadlock is broken'. Both were PARTIAL. The advisory lock was the first blocking point only; removing cancellation's dependency on it fixed one of the two tests and moved the hang, it did not remove it. Recorded here so the earlier, narrower diagnosis is not trusted as complete.

evidence_second_sample.62788: wait_event = ClientRead, blocked_by = {} -- HEAD-OF-LINE HOLDER. Last statement `SELECT record_json, owner_account_id, actor_principal_id, authenticated...` (a resource-scope-columns read). It is IDLE IN TRANSACTION, waiting on the application, not on PostgreSQL.
evidence_second_sample.77436: wait_event = advisory, blocked_by = {95116} -- the advisory waiter is now THIRD in the chain, not the cause.
evidence_second_sample.95116: wait_event = transactionid, blocked_by = {62788} -- waiting for 62788's transaction to end (row-level conflict) while reading model_lane rows.

historical_transaction_across_generation.what_this_means: A transaction that has read lane rows stays open for the entire duration of model inference. Any writer touching those rows blocks on the row lock, and anything needing the execution advisory lock then queues behind that writer. Cancellation is simply the first operation an operator notices, because it is the one they issue while inference is still running.
historical_transaction_across_generation.severity: Architectural and operator-facing. With a real model - not a fixture - inference can run for many seconds to minutes. For that whole window the routing execution's rows are transactionally pinned. This is a scalability and responsiveness defect well beyond the cancellation path.

fix_landed_so_far.1: coordinator.rs spawn admission: the post-cancellation wait on an in-flight factory create is now BOUNDED by config.teardown_timeout instead of unbounded. FIXES ac9_cancel_and_peer_failure_propagate_into_blocked_factory_create, which now passes (35.84s) after previously never terminating.
fix_landed_so_far.2: routing_execution.rs: added active_instance_ids_for_cancellation - a lock-free, integrity-gate-free read of just the active stage instance ids - and cancel_routing_execution now uses it instead of the locking snapshot(). This removes cancellation's FIRST blocking point. The locked snapshot() is unchanged for all other callers, keeping the blast radius on the path that was broken.
fix_landed_so_far.3: Both cancellation tests are bounded with tokio::time::timeout, so a regression reports instead of freezing the whole binary. No assertion was altered.

REMAINING_fix_not_applied.required_change: Stop holding a database transaction across generation. The wave must commit the durable state transition BEFORE awaiting inference and re-open a transaction for the post-generation write, so no lane row is transactionally pinned while a model runs.
REMAINING_fix_not_applied.why_not_attempted_here: This changes transactional boundaries and therefore the atomicity guarantees of the routing terminal path across at least routing_execution.rs and model_lane.rs. It needs the full mixed suite plus the swarm coordinator suites to validate - hours of runtime. Three regressions earlier in this session came from landing boundary changes without that validation, and repeating that pattern on the DURABILITY path would be worse than the defect.
REMAINING_fix_not_applied.concrete_next_step: Identify the transaction opened by the scope-columns read observed on pid 62788 (`SELECT record_json, owner_account_id, actor_principal_id, authenticated...`) and split it at the generation await.

historical_mixed_suite_contention_cascad.headline: The mixed-suite failures CASCADE. Which tests fail or hang depends on scheduling, because one test holding a transaction across generation blocks unrelated tests that touch the same rows. This suite cannot be validated at default parallelism until the transaction boundary is fixed.

evidence_failure_set_is_UNSTABLE.run_B_4_threads_after_fixes: failed = ac9_authority_retry..., ac9_concurrent_production_claims_and_run_extension_are_single_effect_idempotent (NEW), ac9_crash_after_persisted_spawn_intent_recovers_with_new_fence_and_compensation (NEW), ac9_reassignment..., ac9_redispatch..., ac9_replay..., mixed_model_lane_recovery_replays_post_checkpoint... HUNG = ac9_parallel_peer_failure_immediately_cancels_live_sibling (DIFFERENT), mt018_proposal_kind_crdt_message_with_approved_applied_proposal_is_admitted (which PASSED in run A).
evidence_failure_set_is_UNSTABLE.what_the_difference_proves: mt018_proposal_kind_crdt_message_with_approved_applied_proposal_is_admitted passed in run A and hung in run B without any change to it or to CRDT code. A test whose outcome flips purely on scheduling is not reporting its own correctness - it is reporting lock contention. Two ac9 tests likewise appeared as failures only in run B.

historical_mixed_suite_contention_cascad.my_two_fixes_HELD_in_the_full_run: mt009_kernel_crdt_authority_rejects_truncate and mixed_model_lane_recovery_rejects_eventledger_aggregate_mismatch are ABSENT from run B's failure list, confirming the CASCADE truncate fix and the proposal_ref fixture fix hold under full-suite parallelism, not just in isolation.
historical_mixed_suite_contention_cascad.root_cause_is_the_same_one: Recorded in transaction_across_generation_root_cause_2026_08_05: the routing wave holds a PostgreSQL transaction open across model generation. At default parallelism several tests run waves concurrently against the same managed database, so one stalled wave pins rows and every other test needing them queues. That is why the failing/hanging SET moves between runs.
historical_mixed_suite_contention_cascad.VALIDATION_GUIDANCE_until_fixed: Do NOT validate this binary at default parallelism - the result is not reproducible and will accuse innocent tests. Run it with `-- --test-threads=1`, or per-test with --exact, which is how every fix in this session was actually confirmed. This matters for MT-017's capstone, which declares this binary: a capstone run at default parallelism would produce a different failure list each time.
still_genuinely_failing_independent_of_c: ac9_replay_rejects_message_and_artifact_projection_drift - CONFIRMED product defect (replay accepts a tampered artifact projection; the added assertions prove the tamper lands). Reproduces in isolation.
ac9_cancel_terminalizes_parallel_siblings_and_live_sessions - reproduces in isolation; blocked by the transaction-across-generation root cause.

historical_advisory_lock_database_scope_.headline: DEFINITIVE EXPLANATION OF THE MIXED-SUITE CASCADE: PostgreSQL advisory locks are DATABASE-scoped, but this harness isolates tests by SCHEMA inside one shared database. Per-schema isolation therefore does NOT isolate the locks these code paths take, so parallel tests serialize and deadlock across schema boundaries.

the_two_facts_that_combine.1_locks_are_database_wide: pg_advisory_xact_lock keys live in a single per-DATABASE namespace. Two sessions in different schemas of the same database contend on the same key.
the_two_facts_that_combine.2_isolation_is_only_per_schema: Verified directly with psql: the managed cluster has ONE database (`handshake`) containing per-test schemas (mt013_<uuid>, and equivalents for other suites). Confirmed earlier when kernel_process_lifecycle was found once per test schema.

historical_advisory_lock_database_scope_.the_colliding_keyspace: swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs::record_or_extend_run_tx takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0)) keyed on run_id, AND swarm_orchestration/routing_execution.rs::lock_execution takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0)) keyed on execution_id. Same function, same salt (0), same database-wide namespace. record_or_extend_run_tx additionally takes a `SELECT ... FROM model_lane_runs WHERE run_id = $1 FOR UPDATE` row lock in the SAME caller-provided transaction.
why_this_produces_the_observed_symptoms: The failing/hanging SET changes between identical runs, because which test wins a lock depends on scheduling.

mt018_proposal_kind_crdt_message_with_approved_applied_proposal_is_admitted PASSED in one run and HUNG in the next with no change to it or to any CRDT code - it was queued behind another test's transaction, in a different schema.
Single-test runs (--exact) and single-threaded runs are reliable; that is exactly the configuration in which every fix this session was confirmed.

The observed blocking chain (holder idle-in-transaction after a scoped read -> a waiter on `transactionid` -> a waiter on `advisory`) is the model_lane run lock and the routing execution lock interacting.
historical_advisory_lock_database_scope_.relationship_to_the_other_root_cause: This is SEPARATE from, and compounded by, the transaction-across-generation defect recorded in transaction_across_generation_root_cause_2026_08_05. A transaction held open across inference makes the window enormous; database-wide advisory locks make that window affect UNRELATED tests in other schemas. Either alone is survivable; together they make the suite non-deterministic.

actionable_consequences.for_validation_now: Run mixed_model_lane_integration_pg_tests with `-- --test-threads=1` (or per-test --exact). A default-parallelism run is not reproducible and will accuse innocent tests. This is already recorded on MT-017, whose capstone declares this binary.
actionable_consequences.for_the_harness: True isolation requires a DATABASE per test (the task_owned_managed_postgres template mode already creates per-test databases) rather than a schema per test, OR the advisory keys must be namespaced per test schema so they cannot collide across concurrent tests.
actionable_consequences.for_the_product: Split the transaction at the generation await so no lane row and no advisory key is held across inference. Anchor identified: model_lane.rs::record_or_extend_run_tx is called from record_prepared_launch (line 245) inside a caller-controlled transaction.

historical_advisory_lock_database_scope_.verification_method: Two live pg_stat_activity/pg_blocking_pids samples taken DURING the hang windows, plus direct psql inspection of the cluster's database/schema layout. Not inferred from code reading alone.

historical_runtime_flavor_hypothesis_ref.hypothesis: The mixed-suite cancellation tests use `#[tokio::test]`, which is a CURRENT-THREAD runtime, while production runs multi-threaded. A single-threaded executor can manufacture ordering deadlocks (task starvation, lock-holder never polled) that cannot occur in the real product. If so, the defect would be in the TEST HARNESS's runtime flavor, not in the coordinator.
historical_runtime_flavor_hypothesis_ref.experiment: ac9_cancel_terminalizes_parallel_siblings_and_live_sessions was temporarily switched to #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)] and run in isolation with --exact --test-threads=1.
historical_runtime_flavor_hypothesis_ref.RESULT_REFUTED: It FAILED IDENTICALLY: 'cancel_routing_execution must not hang while siblings are live: Elapsed', 81.84s. Executor starvation and single-threaded ordering are therefore RULED OUT. The deadlock reproduces on a multi-threaded runtime, so it is a genuine product-side lock-ordering defect, not a test-harness artifact.
historical_runtime_flavor_hypothesis_ref.probe_reverted: The temporary rename and the flavor attribute were both reverted immediately and verified. This matters: the test is a DECLARED proof target of MT-009 and MT-018, so leaving it renamed would have silently turned two declared proofs into vacuous ones - the exact defect already found on MT-013.
historical_runtime_flavor_hypothesis_ref.value_of_the_negative_result: It removes the cheapest possible explanation. The remaining candidates are all product-side: a transaction held across an await, or a lock-ordering inversion between the wave's run-row locks and the cancellation path. Recorded so the next investigator does not spend the same effort on the runtime flavor.
cumulative_refuted_hypotheses_for_this_h: REFUTED: terminate() never fires the session cancel token (it does - coordinator.rs:4645; the fixture stream polls it every 25ms).
REFUTED: the session teardown await is unbounded (already bounded by teardown_timeout at coordinator.rs:4902).
REFUTED: cancellation's first blocking point (the locking snapshot) was the whole cause - fixing it moved the hang rather than removing it.
REFUTED: current-thread tokio runtime / executor starvation (this experiment).
STILL STANDING: a database transaction is held open while a stage is mid-generation, pinning model_lane_runs rows (advisory + FOR UPDATE via record_or_extend_run_tx) that the cancellation path needs.

historical_SUPERSEDING_POINTER_2026_08_0.headline: The 'STILL STANDING' line above is SUPERSEDED.
